To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance and enjoyment of reading in the ER program varies with proficiency level.

the performance of high and intermediate level readers is better and they enjoy reading more under the intrinsic motivational approach, while low level readers perform better under the extrinsic approach.

1) students' motivation and performance vary with their level of proficiency; 2) high level students are more motivated and perform better in intrinsic conditions, while intermediate level students are more likely to benefit from extrinsic conditions; and 3) low level students benefit from extrinsic requirements and perform well in extrinsic conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of motivation, reading proficiency, and reading performance in ER.
the effects of different motivational requirements on the reading performances of different levels of proficiency.
the relationship between motivation, reading proficiency, and performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
intrinsic motivation is a more effective motivational approach for high level readers while extrinsic motivation is more effective for low level readers in ER programs.
students' motivation, proficiency, and performance interact in a non-linear manner.

students' motivation, proficiency and reading performance are closely linked and that a combination of extrinsic and intrinsic motivation is the most effective approach to maximize students' reading performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

students with higher reading proficiency are more motivated intrinsically, while students with lower reading proficiency are more likely to be motivated extrinsically, and that both types of motivation can be used to enhance students' reading performance.
the performance and enjoyment of students in ER programs vary between proficiency levels and that students should be motivated in a manner that is most suitable for their proficiency levels.
ER programs are an effective tool for improving students' reading performance and enjoyment, and that the effectiveness varies depending on the level of proficiency and motivational requirements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
students' motivation is a key factor in their performance, which should be taken into account when designing ER programs.
teachers need to consider the level of proficiency of students and the type of motivation required when implementing ER programs.
students at different levels of proficiency have different motivational needs and should be treated differently in ER programs.
